items.title: CoreBreak: What a Real AI Agent Flaw Proves About Where Guardrails Belong
items.author: Redpanda Data
items.summary:
At Black Hat 2026, researchers found one structural flaw running through three of the biggest AI agent platforms out there — AWS, Google, and Vercel — and gave it a name: CoreBreak. All three had built their safety measures around the model itself: prompts, filters, refusal training. CoreBreak proved that if you can skip the model, you skip every one of those protections, too.

Tyler Akidau and Marc Millstone walk through how the attack actually worked, why all three vendors landed on the same emergency fix, and what it means that Redpanda had already built that fix into the Agentic Data Plane before the researchers ever published.

items.title: The World Wild Web & Bots With Buying Power
items.author: AAIF Live
items.summary:
An AI slips out of its sandbox. A chatbot won’t explain your cat’s stripes. And your next shopping spree might not involve you clicking anything.

This episode asks whether “dangerously powerful” AI is a security concern, a marketing pitch, or a little of both. Then we put agents to work: booking trips, tackling German paperwork, drawing diagrams, and navigating the chaos of online shopping. Plus: what happens to checkout, advertising, and customer data when your best customer is a bot?

items.title: Key Takeways : Building Databases on top of S3
items.author: The Geek Narrator
items.summary:
**Building a Database on S3: Why Round Trips Are Everything**

What if your database's only durable storage was a plain object storage bucket? In this video I walk through the key ideas behind building systems on top of S3, one idea at a time. We start with the cost math and end with six practical takeaways.

You'll learn:
- Why S3 is roughly 10x cheaper than SSD and 100x cheaper than RAM
- How a write-ahead log and conditional writes give you consistency without a coordinator
- Why you should count round trips, not bytes
- How centroid indexes, huge B-tree nodes, and NVMe caching bring cold queries down to hundreds of milliseconds
- Why S3 can now be the only durable state your system needs

**Chapters**
0:00 Intro: the cost of RAM, SSD, and S3
0:32 The catch: latency and round trips
0:54 The simplest design: a write-ahead log on S3
1:20 Conditional writes and consistency
1:34 Write, read, and space amplification
2:45 Index design for few round trips (HNSW, centroids, B-trees)
3:56 Cold vs. warm queries and caching on NVMe
4:22 Multi-tenancy and noisy neighbors
5:10 Why this is possible now
5:38 Six takeaways
